# lean-pkg gate

validate a lower-tier receipt; gate-pending -&gt; verified-private; records the receipt's lean_toolchain and mathlib_rev as the package's pins.

## Usage

```text
lean-pkg gate --receipt RECEIPT [--comparator PATH] [--refuse-private] [--refuse-dirty]
              [--refresh-formalization] [--agent AGENT] [--check] [--regate]
              [--reason TEXT] [--repo DIR] [common flags] NAME
```

`[common flags]`: `--json`, `--commit`, `--push`, `--no-commit`, also accepted before the command name; see the [CLI overview](../cli.md).

## Arguments and flags

| Argument or flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `NAME` |   |
| `--receipt RECEIPT` | path to receipt JSON. Required. |
| `--comparator PATH` | optional comparator receipt JSON; required later by promote |
| `--refuse-private` | refuse (exit 1, nothing copied) when a receipt holds private strings; default is a WARN line and the receipt is kept |
| `--refuse-dirty` | refuse when tracked files are modified in the checkout; default is a WARN line (receipts are always checked against the bound commit) |
| `--refresh-formalization` | after the gate, regenerate the package's formalization.yaml (derived keys, including status.evidence; kept keys survive) and set its registry pointer; refuses when nothing would change |
| `--agent AGENT` | the agent acting (recorded as the event's actor); another agent's live lease then refuses; with --refresh-formalization: the live lease holder (the file write needs it) |
| `--check` | validate only, against HEAD (with --comparator: both tiers); write nothing, record nothing (works at any status), like `comparator --check` |
| `--regate` | re-gate a verified-private (or public) package on a new receipt in one step: event regated {previous_commit, commit, job_id, reason}, status unchanged; the receipt's commit must descend from the gated commit unless --reason is given |
| `--reason TEXT` | with --regate: accept a receipt commit that does not descend from the gated commit (recorded with non_descendant: true) |
| `--repo DIR` | with --check only: validate against the checkout DIR instead of the registered local_path, for this call (never saved; JSON repo_override). DIR must be a git work tree, and when it has remotes one must be the package's repo. A writing gate refuses it: it binds the registered checkout (move that with `update --path`) |

## Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `gate NAME` | validate a lower-tier receipt; `gate-pending → verified-private`; `--receipt`/`--comparator PATH` is used as given when it exists (relative to the cwd, or absolute); a relative path missing from the cwd but present under the package checkout (or `--check --repo DIR`) is resolved there, announced on stderr, as a `· receipt R resolved against the package checkout: P` line and in JSON `resolved_paths[]` {what, arg, path, base} (the same relative path, never another matching receipt; `comparator NAME` too), else refused naming the caller's cwd, the checkout, both paths tried and the fix; `--check` takes no lease, so `--check --agent` is a usage error (exit 2) that names the writing form; HEAD must be the receipt's commit or an evidence-only descendant of it, or, when the package opted in (`docs_descendants: true`), a docs-only descendant: no build input under the package directory changed ([the rule](../receipts.md#docs-only-descendants-opt-in)); the gated commit stays the receipt's, the text output says `✓ HEAD <c12> is a docs-only descendant of <c12> (N non-build file(s): ...; opted in)`, and the `gate-passed`/`regated` event and `--json` (also `gate --check`, and `comparator` attach/`--check`) carry `descendant_of` and `docs_paths` (up to 50); a refusal under the opt-in names the changed build input(s); without it, a refusal that the docs rule would have admitted adds the hint `update NAME --accept-docs-descendants`; identical re-gate is a no-op; a gate or re-gate records the receipt's `lean_toolchain` and `mathlib_rev` (first 10 characters) into the package's `lean_toolchain` and `mathlib_pin` only when each agrees with the file committed at the receipt's commit (`lean-toolchain`; the mathlib rev in `lake-manifest.json`, prefix-equal); a receipt whose `lean_toolchain` differs from `lean-toolchain`, or whose `mathlib_rev` is not prefix-equal to the mathlib rev in `lake-manifest.json`, committed at its commit is refused (`mathlib mismatch: ...`; `--check` prints `✓ mathlib_rev R = the mathlib rev in lake-manifest.json committed at <c12>`); a package without Mathlib (a readable manifest that lists no `mathlib` package) has the explicit `mathlib_rev` `none`, which is checked (`✓ mathlib_rev none: lake-manifest.json committed at <c12> has no mathlib package`; `none` beside a manifest that pins Mathlib is refused) and leaves `mathlib_pin` null (a recorded pin is cleared); when the manifest is not readable the rev is not checked (`· mathlib_rev not checked: ...`), the recorded pin is kept, the gate still passes, it prints `NAME: pins kept: receipt mathlib_rev X does not match lake-manifest.json at <c12> (unreadable)` and JSON carries `pins_kept` {field: {receipt, manifest}}; a recorded pin that is a prefix of the receipt's rev, or the reverse, is unchanged; it prints `NAME: pins updated from the receipt: lean_toolchain A -> B, mathlib_pin C -> D` when either changes, and adds `pins` {field: {from, to}} to the `gate-passed`/`regated` event (JSON `pins`, `{}` when unchanged); `--check` adds `· pins: gate would record ...` / `· pins kept: ...` and JSON `pins`, `pins_kept`, writing nothing; `--check` also prints `WARN: palomar: not submittable at <c12>: N gap(s) need a new commit (codes); see lean-pkg palomar check NAME --rev <c12>` on stderr when `palomar check` finds error gaps at the receipt's commit (JSON `palomar_check` {ready, commit, errors, warns, codes, command}; null without a readable checkout), never a refusal; `gate` and `--check` print `WARN: toolchain advisory ID: TOOLCHAIN has a known Lean soundness bug, fixed in vX.Y.Z; LINK ...` on stderr for each entry of lean-pkg's toolchain advisories list that names the receipt's `lean_toolchain` (JSON `toolchain_advisories[]` {id, toolchain, summary, fixed_in, links, date_added}, `[]` when none; [toolchain advisories](../receipts.md#checking-a-published-packages-receipts-receipt-check)), never a refusal; on a `verified-private` package plain `gate` is refused and the message names `--regate`; when the package tracks its claims file (`claims_file`, default `claims.yaml`) at the receipt's commit, that committed file (never the working tree) must pass the `claims/1` schema check `claims sync` applies, and every claim's declaration must occur in its file as tracked at that same commit (`claims sync`'s declaration check), else `gate` refuses (exit 1, nothing copied or recorded; the message names `claims check --file` for schema errors or `claims sync` for missing declarations, and says the fix is a new commit, so a new receipt and a re-gate); the tree at the receipt's commit must not let the build read sources outside the package directory, which the receipt does not bind (see [Path dependencies](../receipts.md#path-dependencies)): a committed symlink whose target is absolute or has a `..` component is refused, and so is one that resolves into `.lean-receipts/` or to the recorded `formalization_yaml` (chains and directory symlinks followed; evidence there may change later, so the build would read unbound bytes), and so is a `path` package in `lake-manifest.json` committed there whose `dir` leaves the package directory (absolute, or `..` after normalising), or which is, or passes through, a symlink, a submodule (gitlink) or a directory not tracked at that commit (such as `.lake/`), or which contains a gitlink; each refusal names the entry (a tracked directory inside the package is accepted; a manifest that is not valid JSON is refused; `--check` prints `✓ lake-manifest.json at <commit12>: no path dependency outside the package directory` and `✓ no symlink at <commit12> leaves the package directory or points into .lean-receipts/`); `report_sha256` must equal the SHA-256 of the redacted verify log `<c12>-<job slug>-verify.redacted.log` wherever a copy is found (beside the `--receipt` file, in the package's `.lean-receipts/`, tracked there at HEAD), else refused (`report_sha256 mismatch: ...`); a `NAME.gz` copy (`receipt --compress-log`) is stream-decompressed and its uncompressed bytes must hash to `report_sha256` (never the `.gz` hash), the `.gz` to `report_compressed.sha256` and the length equal `report_compressed.bytes` when recorded, output past that length refused (gzip-bomb guard; 4 GiB without `report_compressed`); `✓ report_sha256 = sha256 of NAME (where)` (`where, decompressed from .gz` for a `.gz`) in the text output; none found, or a copy that cannot be read, is refused (`report log missing: NAME ...`, naming where it looked and the path to restore it to; [Restoring preserved evidence](../receipts.md#restoring-preserved-evidence)), JSON `report_log` {checked, log, where[], copy[]}; the sealed log found beside `--receipt` is copied into `.lean-receipts/` beside the canonical receipt when no copy is there (`copy[]`; `--check` prints `· gate would also copy ...`), so the stored receipt verifies on its own; every check on both copies (the receipt and, with `--comparator`, the comparator receipt) runs before either is written, so a refusal writes nothing to `.lean-receipts/`, and `gate`/`comparator` refuse to write when `.lean-receipts` or the destination file is a symlink; success prints `✓ claims.yaml at <commit12>: schema ok (N claims), declarations found` or a neutral `· no claims.yaml tracked at <commit12>`, and JSON gains `claims_schema` {checked, commit, file, ok, claims, errors[], declarations {checked, ok, problems[]}} (`ok` null when `checked` is false); receipt bytes (keys and values) are scanned for private local paths before the copy into `.lean-receipts/` (stderr `WARN: receipt field F contains a private local path (kept: ...; --refuse-private refuses such a receipt)`, worded for what happened to the receipt: `kept` when it was accepted, `nothing copied (--check)` under `--check`, `nothing copied: refused for another reason, below` only when the gate refused; `private_strings` in JSON); `lean-toolchain` is read at the receipt's commit; modified tracked files print a `WARN` (`dirty` in JSON); a checkout off its default branch or detached prints `WARN: evaluating branch X, not the default D` on stderr, never a refusal; after recording, each evidence file git ignores prints a stderr `WARN: PATH is git-ignored (RULE): ...` with the remedy (`ignored_evidence[]` {path, rule} in JSON; see `promote`) | `--receipt PATH` `[--comparator PATH]` `[--refuse-private]` (refuse, exit 1, nothing copied) `[--refuse-dirty]` `[--refresh-formalization [--agent A]]` (then regenerate `formalization.yaml`, derived keys including `status.evidence`, and set its pointer in one step; another agent's live lease and a kept key failing the schema refuse before the gate; an identical re-gate whose file is already current is refused with nothing written; `--json` gains `"formalization": {path, written, unchanged, registry_updated, validation, placeholders}`) `[--regate [--reason TEXT]]` (re-gate a `verified-private` package, or a `public` one, on a new receipt in one step instead of `update --status gate-pending` then `gate`: the same validations as `gate` (binding, toolchain, sorry, axioms, the claims file at the receipt's commit, the comparator binding when `--comparator` is given), status unchanged, one `regated` event {previous_commit, commit, job_id, checker, receipt, reason, non_descendant?}, so one registry commit and push in committed mode; the receipt's commit must descend from the commit of the recorded gate receipt (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`), else refused with nothing copied unless `--reason` is given, which records `non_descendant: true`; refused on any other status, or with no recorded gate receipt; `--reason` without `--regate` is a usage error, exit 2; prints `NAME: <status>, re-gated <prev12> -> <commit12>`; JSON `event: regated`, `previous_commit`, `non_descendant`, `reason`; with `--check` the same checks write nothing and add a `✓ regate:`/`✗ regate:` line and JSON `regate` {previous_commit, non_descendant}) `[--check]` (read-only: every validation `gate` makes, against HEAD, with `--comparator` both tiers; prints `✓` lines for binding, the `formalization.yaml` derived-only rule, toolchain at the bound commit, sorry count and axioms, and the claims file at the receipt's commit (`✓ … schema ok (N claims)`, `✗ claims.yaml at <commit12>: <first error>` with exit 1, or `·` when none is tracked), or the refusal `gate` would print; writes nothing, records no event, works at any status, exit 0/1; JSON `event: gate-checked`, `recorded: false`, `checks[]`, `head`, `comparator`, `claims_schema`; `ok: false` on a failing claims file) `[--check --repo DIR]` (validate against the checkout `DIR` instead of the registered `local_path`, for this one call: never written to the registry; a stderr note `using --repo DIR instead of the registered local_path ...`; JSON `repo_override` {path, registered_path, remote_match}, `null` without `--repo`; `DIR` must be a git work tree, and when it has remotes and the record names a repository one remote must be it (`remote_match: true`), otherwise the caller vouches for it; a writing `gate` refuses `--repo` (exit 2): a gate binds the registered checkout, which `update --path` moves). A successful gate (and `publish --yes`) ends with a `results-ledger:` line naming `lean-pkg status NAME` and `lean-pkg claims ledger NAME` (JSON `rl_reminder: true`, `rl_hint`): lean-pkg keeps no results ledger; see [Results ledger](../lifecycle.md#results-ledger) |

## Exit codes

0 success (dry runs and no-ops included), 1 refused or failed, 2 usage error; see [Exit codes](../cli.md#exit-codes).

Exit 1 is also a negative answer here:

- `gate NAME --check`: `gate` would refuse this receipt

## JSON output

Top-level keys of `--json`, as recorded in the golden contract (tests/golden/json-keys.json):

- `gate` (exit 0): `claims_schema`, `commit`, `dirty`, `event`, `gate`, `ignored_evidence`, `name`, `ok`, `pins`, `pins_kept`, `private_strings`, `receipt`, `report_log`, `resolved_paths`, `rl_hint`, `rl_reminder`, `status`, `status_unchanged`, `toolchain_advisories`
- `gate-check` (exit 0): `checks`, `claims_schema`, `commit`, `comparator`, `dirty`, `event`, `head`, `name`, `ok`, `palomar_check`, `pins`, `pins_kept`, `private_strings`, `recorded`, `repo_override`, `report_log`, `resolved_paths`, `status`, `toolchain_advisories`

## Examples

Validate the receipt against HEAD and record nothing; exit 1 when gate would refuse it.

```bash
lean-pkg gate my-proof --receipt .lean-receipts/receipt.json --check
```

Accept the lower-tier receipt and move the package from gate-pending to verified-private.

```bash
lean-pkg gate my-proof --receipt .lean-receipts/receipt.json
```

Re-gate an already verified package on a newer receipt; the status does not change.

```bash
lean-pkg gate my-proof --receipt .lean-receipts/receipt.json --regate
```
